correctness.rationale: For every fixed R>0, single-disk diagonalization gives ℓ0=1-e^{-R}, ℓ1=1-(1+R)e^{-R}, gap Re^{-R}; coherent states have exact overlap s=e^{-πd²/2}. The separated-disk trace bound Tr(B+B-)≤R²e^{-π(d-2√(R/π))²} bounds the nonleading sector. The opposite-disk leakage q≤Re^{-π(d-√(R/π))²} bounds the squared complement coupling. The exact even/odd compression has eigenvalues (ℓ0+q±2ℓ0s)/(1±s); an explicit Schur-complement estimate transfers these to the two largest eigenvalues with O_R(q), and parity controls the modes. Since q=o(s), the stated coefficient and gap are rigorous. The independently coded numerical matrix checker passed 56 assertions; it is supplementary rather than an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The full source text of the 2022 Gaussian localization norm paper, the 2021 Faber–Krahn work, the 2024 stability analysis, and a 2024 nonradial Fock Toeplitz norm result were examined for the same objects and implications. Their conclusions bound or optimize a single largest norm or supply one-disk spectra; none of their stated results supplies the area-dependent exponential coefficient, both eigenvalues, and parity-resolved modes for two fixed-area disks at large separation. Targeted literature and repository searches found no equivalent claim. Historical priority is provisional, as a broad double-well Toeplitz theorem with an unstated specialization may exist.
residual_risks: General anti-Wick/Toeplitz semiclassical multiwell tunneling theorems may specialize to this fixed-area distant-disk scaling; absence of a located match is not proof of uniqueness.

value.rationale: Two disjoint observation apertures represent a natural two-channel concentration problem with nearly degenerate localized coherent states; neither a single-disk norm nor a global mask-size inequality quantifies the conditioning of the resulting two-dimensional top spectral space. The exact exponential tunneling coefficient, parity-resolved signals and residual spectral gap together determine the mode ambiguity and its separation dependence. The statement is a structural fixed-area asymptotic, not a minor numerical constant or arbitrary finite experiment.
